neighbours.label: something valued being weighed or put at stake: health, safety, future or livelihood of people, in 'X is worth more than ...' / 'your future depends on it' arguments
fire: Do your homework before you invest, because your whole retirement could be riding on this choice.
No quarterly profit is worth the health of the workers who breathe those fumes.
What matters more, the convenience of a few drivers or the safety of the children crossing that road?
Remember that your livelihood is on the line every time the market opens.
They traded the long-term health of the river for a few years of cheap electricity.
It's your family's future, so don't let a salesman rush you into signing.
Is a faster commute really worth the lives of the people living along the highway?
Short-term savings should never come before the wellbeing of the patients in our care.
quiet: Do your homework before the exam, because the questions cover every chapter.
The quarterly profit report shows the factory produced more fumes filters than last year.
Drivers can use the new road, and children cross it at the marked crossing.
Remember that the market opens at nine and closes at half past four.
The river supplies water to a dam that produces cheap electricity.
The salesman showed my family three different cars before lunch.
The new highway shortens the commute for people who live along it.
The hospital saved money by buying supplies in bulk for its patients.

notes: Card top examples: 'your financial future', 'the health and lives of the many', 'the safety of other people'. Probe: 'health of our children' (worth-more) 1.03, 'your financial future depends' 0.81, neutral 'future of the product line' 0.00.
